answer: An agent marketplace can resist sybils by making new identity weight climb a steep reputation ridge: only job receipts signed by established, non-kin counterparties mint admission credits, and each credit expires after a few epochs. Credits cannot be pooled across cloned keys, so a farm never reaches the zenith of bidding power without real counterparty work. Sponsors also lock a slow-thaw glacier of stake that burns if the newcomer is slashed, forcing an attacker to fund fresh outsider receipts and risk capital for every fake ID.
